title: A SIMPLE-recovery log file that is huge but nearly empty: shrink it once
symptom: A database log file is many GB on disk while almost none of it is used. 27 Oct: KorEmailIndex_log.ldf was 10,183 MB with 6 MB used, in D:\SQLData on KOR-APP01\SQLEXPRESS.
cause: A one-off large load or long transaction grew the log once; under SIMPLE recovery the space is reused but never handed back to the disk. It is not a fault that recurs nightly.
check: As sysadmin in that database: SELECT total_log_size_in_bytes, used_log_space_in_bytes FROM sys.dm_db_log_space_usage; and size*8/1024 from sys.master_files. Confirm recovery_model_desc = SIMPLE and that no heavy work is running on that database.
fix: When nothing heavy is running: DBCC SHRINKFILE (N'<logical log name>', 1024) once, then read both numbers again. 27 Oct 17:11: 10,183 MB -> 1,031 MB (sys.master_files 1,032 MB), mdf untouched, about 9.1 GB back on D:. Do not schedule shrinks; if the log grows back to the same size, find the transaction that grows it instead. Proof: board row 36.
plain: Remembers how a mostly-empty 10 GB database log on APP01 was safely cut to 1 GB, and when not to repeat it.
